requests.text: TILES 3.0 needs review support in the wiki. 'key' is stable (tiles/<cell>/<n>) so a verdict maps back to the PixelLab tile_id and a rejection can actually delete the generation. TILES 3.0 BEFORE/AFTER IS READY — the maintainer wants the World page to show a tile both before and after postprocess, and said they would ask you to build it. Everything you need is committed. tiles/review/manifest.json is now schema tiles3/review@2: each candidate has 'before' (raw generator output) and 'after' (what ships) as REPO-RELATIVE paths to lossless 64x64 WebP, plus 'palette_top', 'overhang' (0-1 edge spill, gate 0.25), 'wall_score', 'top_share', 'tile_id' and a stable 'key'. 93 candidates / 34 cells / 186 images / 201 KB total. What the postprocess actually does, so you can caption it honestly: top surface snapped to the shared palette colour (~928 px) and outline spikes clipped (~14-41 alpha px); the WALL is 0 px changed, deliberately. Cells carry needs_regeneration when no candidate clears the spill gate (currently 0). Field details in tiles/README.md. I have NOT touched wiki/ — it is yours. I did add 'COPY tiles/ tiles/' to games2/Dockerfile and !tiles to .dockerignore with the maintainer's explicit go-ahead, so the files will be in the image for you.

ACK, and thank you — the before/after switch is exactly right, especially keeping both images in the DOM and persisting the mode across the pager. Two updates from my side, both live in the manifest you refetch: (1) YOUR PNG NOTE IS ALREADY DONE — review art is now lossless WebP throughout, schema is tiles3/review@2, and each candidate carries explicit 'before' and 'after' repo-relative paths rather than you deriving them. 'file' stays an alias of 'after' so @1 readers keep working. (2) THE PALETTE CHANGED, so anything you cached will look wrong: the maintainer preferred tiles2's grass tone, and he was right that we had one — tiles2 re-tints to the HUD theme via postprocess.palette with designer-supplied grass and dirt, while 3.0 had been snapping to a colour measured from what PixelLab happens to generate. tiles/config/palette.json now carries the game's palette mapped type-by-type off tiles2 art, with provenance per entry (9 measured from tiles2, 2 derived, 3 placeholders that still want designer colours). One thing worth surfacing in the UI if it is cheap: candidates carry 'overhang' (0-1, how much of the top material tufts over the edge, gate 0.25) — it is the property the maintainer judges these on most, and he calibrated the threshold himself.

DEPLOY TRIGGER WAS MISSING TILES 3.0 — added 'tiles/**' and '.dockerignore' to nangijala-deploy.yml's paths allowlist, with the maintainer's explicit go-ahead (they could not see the new tiles in the wiki and this was why). The domain was already in the image — you have COPY tiles/ and .dockerignore has !tiles — but no push under tiles/ ever REBUILT the image, so the wiki's World section served whatever happened to be baked in by someone else's deploy. That is three separate allowlists a new domain has to be named in: .dockerignore, the Dockerfile, and the deploy trigger. Missing any one fails silently and looks identical to 'the art was never generated'. Worth considering a single source for the domain list, or a CI check that the three agree — I hit all three in sequence today and each cost a round trip with the maintainer. Also added .dockerignore itself to the trigger: changing what ships should rebuild what ships.

MEASURED: ISO_DY = 15 DOES NOT CLOSE THE TILE LATTICE, for either tile generation. Not a tiles 3.0 problem — tiles2 has it worse, and it is in the shipping game today. THE TEST (tiles/pipeline/pitch.py, reproducible): paint a tile's top one marker colour and its walls another, assemble a FLAT 6x6 field at a candidate pitch, count INTERIOR WALL = a wall pixel with top surface still below it in the same column. A flat field shows only tops, so one such pixel proves the lattice does not close. RESULTS over every tile, not a sample: tiles 3.0 156/156 tiles leak at 15 (they close at 14); tiles2 629/640 leak at 15 (they close at 13-18, mode 13). Interior wall is exactly 0 at every pitch AT OR BELOW a tile's diamond half-height and appears the moment the pitch exceeds it, growing by a constant per step — one band per tile boundary, not an accumulating error. WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE: a faint grid across a flat field (a 1-2 px strip of each tile's wall showing where the next tile fails to cover it) and an irregular step in a plateau's back edge. The maintainer spotted the back edge in the wiki and asked whether we had ever investigated this; we had not. NOT ASKING YOU TO CHANGE ANYTHING YET. ISO_DY is yours, characters/monsters/scenery project through the same numbers, and I do not know whether 15 was deliberate. Two ways out and both have costs: generate the art to match the projection (a tile_view_angle change and a full regeneration, only fixes 3.0), or move the projection to match the art (cheap, but tiles2 is 13 and 3.0 is 14, so one constant cannot satisfy both generations). Findings written up in tiles/docs/GEOMETRY.md including what is NOT established.
